thread:
jess_customer-success: FYI we just got a high-priority escalation from Aurora — p99 token latency up ~3x since last night, customers seeing timeouts and retries. They reported spikes during 03:00-04:30 UTC. Attachment had a sample request id 0a1b2c3d.

sam_support: Can confirm — I forwarded logs and a repro curl from their SRE. They said it started after our auto-rollout yesterday evening.

jess_customer-success: Key asks: 1) what's causing the tail? 2) quick mitigations (can we throttle or route away?) 3) ETA to fix. Aurora is threatening to throttle traffic if not resolved.

kai_sre: I'm starting with tenant-level metrics. Pushing a quick grafana snapshot, looks like their backend queue depth for model x-llama-13b increased sharply at 02:48 UTC and stayed noisy. Per-tenant concurrency for aurora-tenant spiked from 4 -> 18 for short bursts.

lex_runtime: That aligns with a noisy-neighbor signature — continuous batching got overwhelmed by long-running requests. Do we have the request traces?

sam_support: Uploaded their repro curl (sanitized) and logs to the thread: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \
  -d '{"input":"long prompt ..."}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
Their request latency sample: 12s, 18s, timeout at 30s.

kai_sre: Poking traces — trace 0a1b2c3d shows repeated large attention windows, cache miss pattern, and a model fallback attempt to 8-bit variant which increased CPU on the worker host. Host i-0f... shows 95th CPU at 90% during the spike.

lex_runtime: Hm. Two hypotheses: 1) Aurora started a burst of high-seq-length requests (long context) causing KV cache misses and long GPU kernels; 2) there's a pod that's underprovisioned causing queueing.

maria_product: Quick Q: did we roll any model config or kernel change yesterday? I remember a small runtime patch to improve batching coalescing went out.

ci_deploy_bot: deploy_bot: Deployment 2026-06-15T18:12:03Z rolled: runtime-service v2.14.7 -> v2.14.8 by @lex_runtime.

kai_sre: That matches timeline. I'm going to rollback the runtime config for affected pool to v2.14.7 for aurora-tenant routing only — doing a canary now on two hosts. Will update in ~5m.

lex_runtime: A note on the patch: it changed batching heuristics to be more aggressive on prefix merging, which can increase single-request GPU time for very long sequences. We underestimated tail impact for mixed sequence workloads.

sam_support: Aurora said they occasionally batch long generative prompts (user transcripts), so that would match.

kai_sre: Canary rollback applied to hosts h-201 and h-203 at 1782005000. Observing p99 drop from 12s -> 3.2s on those hosts. Rolling to remaining pool now.

ops_bot: ops: Tenant-level temporary throttle applied for aurora-tenant: rate_limit=30rps, burst=80 at 1782005400. Config id rl-aurora-1782.

jess_customer-success: Communicated to Aurora: temporary throttle + rollback in progress, asked for their help to send sample traffic for validation.

maria_product: For a medium-term fix, propose: add per-tenant max-inflight to protect from long-seq jobs, and an allowlist for heavy-sequence workloads so we route them to a dedicated pool. Also add a telemetry flag to surface sequence-length distributions per-tenant.

lex_runtime: Agreed. Action items: (1) revert heuristic change for mixed workloads and draft a safer variant (PR opened), (2) add per-tenant max-inflight and cap for long-seq ops, (3) expose seq-length histogram in console. I can get (1) done in a hotfix by EOD, (2) and (3) will be next sprint but we can hotpatch per-tenant policy as a stop-gap.

kai_sre: Monitoring shows p99 back to baseline across pool after full rollback at 1782006600. I'll keep a watch window until 1782008600.

sam_support: Aurora validated on staging and production — they saw reduced tail and will escalate internally to remove threat to throttle. They also asked for an allowlist so heavy-seq traffic is routed to a dedicated pool.

jess_customer-success: Logging ask: please capture the exact request ids and timestamps for Aurora so we can include in the postmortem. Also prep a short customer-facing note (2-3 sentences) explaining root cause and what we did.

maria_product: I'll draft the customer note. Suggest language: "We identified a regression introduced by a runtime batching heuristic that increased tail latency for certain high-sequence workloads. We rolled back the change and applied protective per-tenant throttles; we are implementing dedicated routing for long-sequence workloads."

kai_sre: Postmortem checklist: compile traces (we have 0a1b2c3d + 0a1b2c3e..g), timeline, mitigation (rollback + throttle), RCA, and follow-ups (per-tenant max-inflight, allowlist routing, seq-length telemetry). I'll own the postmortem.

ops_bot: ops: Throttle rl-aurora-1782 removed at 1782008800 after customer validation.

sam_support: Customer happy for now, asked for weekly updates until allowlist is in place.

jess_customer-success: Great work all. Please add all artifacts to the postmortem doc and tag @maria_product when ready. Closing watch window in 30m if stable. :thumbsup:
